div.head: Cn 1027 5
div.ab: Sit autem uobis notum, quia magna congregatio nobilium in ipsa pascali solennitate ibi cum domino papa Iohanne et imperatore Cuonrado erat, scilicet omnes principes gentium a monte Gargano usque ad istud proximum mare, qui omnes me et honorifice suscepere et donis pretiosis honorauere; maxime autem ab imperatore donis uariis et muneribus pretiosis honoratus sum, tam in uasis aureis et argenteis quam in palliis et uestibus ualde pretiosis.

Sit autem vobis notum, quia magna congregatio nobilium in ipsa pascali solennitate ibi cum domino papa Iohanne et imperatore Cuonrado erat, scilicet omnes principes gentium a monte Gargano usque ad istud proximum mare, qui omnes me et honorifice suscepere et donis pretiosis honoravere; maxime autem ab imperatore donis variis et muneribus pretiosis honoratus sum, tam in vasis aureis et argenteis quam in palliis et vestibus valde pretiosis.

Now be it known to you that there was a great assembly of nobles there at the celebration of Easter with my lord the Pope John and the Emperor Conrad, namely, all the princes of the nations from Mount Garganus to the sea which is nearest [to us], all of whom received me graciously and honoured me with costly gifts; but chiefly was I honoured by the Emperor with various gifts and costly presents, both vessels of gold and silver and mantles and very costly robes.

Be it known to you, that there was there a great assembly of nobles at the celebration of Easter, with the lord Pope John and the Emperor Conrad, namely all the princes of the nations from Mount Garganus to the sea nearest [to us]; and they all both received me with honour and honoured me with precious gifts; but especially was I honoured by the emperor with various gifts and costly presents, with vessels of gold and silver as well as silk robes and very costly garments.
div.note: Latin only (Cnut's letter of 1027, c. May; Latin translation c. 1070–1100, the Old English original is lost). Liebermann's text is from Florence of Worcester (ed. MGH SS XIII 126), compared with Ox (Oxford, Corpus 157 p. 329) and William of Malmesbury II 183; text in column T. Liebermann gives no German translation.

note.label: [to us]
note.seg: Cnut composed this letter on his homeward journey to Denmark, perhaps, as Liebermann suggests, in Flanders or Hamburg. The nearest sea would therefore be the North Sea.

div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 276 (November 2026; read twice from the page images and against the text layer). His superscript letters, which refer to his Erklärungen, are left out.

note.seg: Über Konrads Kaiserkrönung durch Johann XIX. zu Ostern und die Römische Synode am 6. April s. Jaffé-Löw. Reg. pont. I 516 f. Nur Wipo gedenkt Cnuts. Cnut stand freundschaftlich zu Conrad vielleicht schon seit 1025; Bresslau I 102

On Conrad's imperial coronation by John XIX at Easter and the Roman synod of 6 April see Jaffé-Löw. Reg. pont. I 516 f. Only Wipo mentions Cnut. Cnut was on friendly terms with Conrad perhaps already from 1025; Bresslau I 102

Monte Gargano, province of Foggia, north of Sipontum

Nordsee, nicht das Rom nahe Meer, wie Giesebrecht und Larson verstehen. Da er laut 13 denselben Weg hin wie her reiste, so kann er z. B. in Flandern (s. o. 2b) schreiben oder zu Hamburg, das er hin- oder herreisend besucht hat; Adam Brem. II 58; vgl. Bresslau I 103. Über die damals gewohnten Reisewege von England nach Italien vgl. Schulte Gesch. mittelalterl. Verkehrs I 67

The North Sea, not the sea near Rome, as Giesebrecht and Larson understand it. Since according to 13 he travelled the same way there as back, he may be writing e.g. in Flanders (see above 2b) or at Hamburg, which he visited on the way there or back; Adam Brem. II 58; cf. Bresslau I 103. On the customary routes of that time from England to Italy cf. Schulte Gesch. mittelalterl. Verkehrs I 67

Die Heiratsverbindung zwischen Cnuts Tochter Gunhilde und Konrads Sohn Heinrich (III.) war noch nicht in Aussicht genommen, vielleicht aber die Abtretung der Dänenmark Schleswig an Dänemark. Abgeschlossen ward beides erst 1035; Steenstrup III 356; Bresslau II 144. 234. 345 f. Dieser sieht das Ziel des Bundes für Deutschland in der Unterwerfung der Ostseewenden. Zu Handelsverträgen fühlte Cnut besonderen Anlass, als Beherrscher der seefahrenden Nationen; s. Gl Handel 17; international 5

The marriage alliance between Cnut's daughter Gunhild and Conrad's son Henry (III) was not yet in prospect, but perhaps the cession of the Danish March, Schleswig, to Denmark was. Both were concluded only in 1035; Steenstrup III 356; Bresslau II 144. 234. 345 f. The latter sees the aim of the alliance, for Germany, in the subjugation of the Baltic Wends. Cnut had special reason for trade agreements, as ruler of the seafaring nations; see Glossary Handel 17; international 5
